fullPassage: Here's an application of metaphors to research papers: Below-grade-level readers in my urban middle school have a great deal of difficulty doing research. Their answer when assigned to do "a report" is to come to the media center and copy verbatim everything in the encyclopedia article or whatever source they have located, be it Internet, print, or whatever. To try to get the students to understand why it isn't necessary to copy everything in the articles, I use a comparison to a supermarket. I ask them if everything in the supermarket is useful, and we discuss this, with the usual conclusion being that it does, but we don't buy everything all the time. Then I ask them why they don't buy everything each time they go and how they determine what to buy when they go with their parents. Someone usually mentions that they have a list. From that point on, I lead a discussion about how whatever their teachers have asked for is their "shopping list" for their research, and they should just read for that information and write it down in note format. It sometimes helps them to understand that copying everything is a wasteful endeavor.

det.korean: 원래 사용된 것과 정확히 같은 말을 사용하여 = 축어적으로(verbatim).
det.analysis:
✅ ① verbatim: 축어적으로, 영영풀이와 일치
❌ ③ virtually: 사실상, 거의
❌ ② versatile: 다재다능한
❌ ④ verbose: 장황한
det.tip: verbatim(축어적으로): verb-(말) + -atim(그대로) = 말 그대로. verbose(장황한)와 혼동 주의.

det.tip: conclude(결론짓다/동사) → conclusion(결론/명사). 'the usual conclusion being ~'

questions.passage: Here's an application of metaphors to research papers: Below-grade-level readers in my urban middle school have a great deal of difficulty doing research. Their answer when assigned to do "a report" is to come to the media center and copy verbatim everything in the encyclopedia article or whatever source they have located, be it Internet, print, or whatever. To try to get the students to understand why it isn't necessary to copy everything in the articles, ____. I ask them if everything in the supermarket is useful, and we discuss this, with the usual conclusion being that it does, but we don't buy everything all the time. Then I ask them why they don't buy everything each time they go and how they determine what to buy when they go with their parents. Someone usually mentions that they have a list. From that point on, I lead a discussion about how whatever their teachers have asked for is their "shopping list" for their research, and they should just read for that information and write it down in note format. It sometimes helps them to understand that copying everything is a wasteful endeavor.

ch: I use a comparison to a supermarket

det.analysis:
✅ ② I use a comparison to a supermarket: 원문 일치 — 슈퍼마켓 비유로 선택적 정보 수집 설명
❌ ① assign a different topic: 원문에 없음
❌ ④ restrict Internet: 원문에 없음
❌ ③ cite sources: 인용법이 아닌 정보 선별이 핵심
det.tip: comparison(비교, 비유): 슈퍼마켓에서 모든 것을 사지 않듯이 연구에서도 모든 것을 베끼지 않는다는 비유.
